input.topic: Intern IGNORED CEO's Emails, Got a RAISE?!

script.fullText: I ignored my CEO's emails... and got a raise. Everyone told me I was crazy, career suicide. But I knew something they didn't about power dynamics. The CEO only emailed me about trivial stuff, micromanaging my time. Replying instantly validated his ego, not my work. So I started responding slower, sometimes not at all. Suddenly, my projects were getting more attention and resources. He realized I was prioritizing tasks, not his every whim. Perceived value increased. This is called "strategic unavailability." But if they're busy, you hang on their every word. I used this principle to reclaim my time and boost my perceived worth. The CEO noticed the improved output, finally saw my value, and... bam! Raise! Don't be a doormat. Control your availability. Strategic unavailability is a game changer. Want more insider secrets to climb the corporate ladder?
